_comment: PDF-96 D5/D6. The two contracts as data: the exit-code contract and the output contract (both re-derived from src/pdf_tooling/cli/exit_codes.py, README.md's ## Output contract and ## Exit codes), plus the atomic-write sequence (re-derived from src/pdf_tooling/safety/atomic.py, compressed from PLAN.md §5.3's seven steps to six stations). tests/test_website_diagrams.py pins the exit-code half against ALL_EXIT_CODES; the atomic-write half is not independently re-derivable from source (it is prose about a sequence, not a walk), so it is authored here and reviewed, not asserted numerically beyond its station count and its ordering.

codes.name: OK
codes.meaning: Success — including an empty-but-valid report. A --dry-run mirrors the code the real run would return, so it is not always 0.

codes.name: FAILURE
codes.meaning: The operation ran and failed — corrupt input, engine error, unwritable destination.

codes.name: USAGE
codes.meaning: Bad invocation — unknown flag, mutually exclusive flags, malformed page range, unknown subcommand.

codes.name: ENGINE_MISSING
codes.meaning: A required engine or binary is unavailable. The message always carries an install hint.

codes.name: NO_INPUT
codes.meaning: Valid invocation, nothing to act on.

codes.name: AUTH
codes.meaning: Password required, incorrect, or of the wrong kind.

carveOuts.title: The carve-out on code 0, an engine's verdict
carveOuts.text: convert and ocr hand the operand to an out-of-process binary — soffice or tesseract — and a --dry-run may not start either. Every dry item of those verbs carries engine_verified: false in its detail, so the preview never reads as an unqualified success.

carveOuts.title: The carve-out on code 0, a password's correctness
carveOuts.text: Whether a password can be resolved is decidable from existence alone and a preview predicts it; whether a resolved password is correct is decidable only by trying it, and a preview must not become an oracle. Every dry item that names a password source carries password_verified: false in its detail.

rules: Add a code; never renumber one.
Breaking this table is a major version bump, not a patch.

shapes.behaviour: An aligned, plain-text table for a person reading a terminal.
One object per item, one per line — each line carrying its own schema_version.

outputContract.asymmetry: Errors are the one deliberate asymmetry: with -o table an error is a one-line message on stderr, but with -o json or -o ndjson it is an object on stdout, so a machine consumer reading stdout never has to also read stderr to learn a run failed.

stations.name: Plan / refuse
stations.detail: Refuses an existing target without --force. Exit 5.

stations.name: Dry-run gate
stations.detail: Returns before any filesystem call, in both modes.

stations.name: Temp file
stations.detail: A temp file beside the target, on the same filesystem — which is what makes the rename atomic.

stations.name: os.replace()
stations.detail: Atomic. The only place the two tracks touch.

atomicWrite.failure: Anything fails at steps ① through ⑤: the temp is unlinked, your file is untouched, and the process exits with a non-zero code.
